name: N0tail (Johan Sundstein)
milestone_by_age_26: Won The International 2018 and 2019 back-to-back with OG, becoming the highest-earning esports player in history (~$7.1M+ in prize money) by age 26; also won four Dota Major championships and multiple DreamHack titles in Heroes of Newerth before transitioning to Dota 2.
early_history_summary: Sundstein began playing video games at age two and became one of the youngest professional Heroes of Newerth players at 15, teaming up with Fly and NoVa to form a squad sponsored by Fnatic. He won four consecutive DreamHack events in HoN before transitioning to Dota 2 with Fnatic in 2012, and co-founded OG in 2015.
family_context_summary: Born in Denmark to Faroese parents; his grandfather was Jógvan Sundstein, former Faroese prime minister, suggesting a politically connected family background. Sundstein left high school early to pursue esports full-time.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources that parents had gaming or tech domain expertise, though the family's political prominence (grandfather was PM) suggests a supportive, resource-connected household.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Fnatic sponsorship, Fly partnership, HoN prodigy, early competitive scene
evidence_summary: N0tail became a professional HoN player at 15, was recruited by Fnatic, and won four consecutive DreamHack titles before transitioning to Dota 2. His grandfather was a former Faroese prime minister, suggesting a politically connected family. His long-standing partnership with Fly and the Fnatic organizational pipeline provided elite ecosystem access. He co-founded OG in 2015 and won back-to-back TIs in 2018-2019, becoming the highest-earning esports player. The structural wave of esports' growth and his early specialization in MOBAs were key leverage engines.

He bounced through multiple teams (mTw, Sigma, Denial, Alliance) with mixed results before becoming OG's coach in 2016, where he oversaw four Major wins, then transitioned to player to win TI 2018 and 2019.

He started his professional career at 16 playing DotA for mousesports, where he met Puppey, beginning a long-standing partnership. He transitioned to Dota 2 and competed at TI 2011, eventually joining Na'Vi in 2013 and forming Team Liquid in 2015.

He joined Na'Vi in 2010 and won the inaugural TI in 2011, then founded Team Secret in 2014.

name: SumaiL (Syed Sumail Hassan)
milestone_by_age_26: Won The International 2015 with Evil Geniuses at age 16, becoming the youngest player ever to win TI and the youngest esports player to earn over $1M in prize money; also won DAC 2015 — all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Hassan was born in Karachi, Pakistan, and started playing Dota at age 8, often traveling to internet cafes on a small motorbike and even selling his bicycle to afford gaming time. His family moved to Rosemont, Illinois in 2012, where he joined the North American Elite League and became its highest-rated player. Evil Geniuses signed him in January 2015, and he won TI 2015 in August of that year.
family_context_summary: Born in Karachi, Pakistan; has an older brother YawaR who also plays professional Dota 2. Family moved to the United States (Rosemont, Illinois) in 2012 to seek better opportunities. Family faced resource constraints in Pakistan, with Sumail selling his bicycle to afford internet cafe time.

name: Hungrybox (Juan Manuel DeBiedma)
category: Super Smash Bros. Melee esports pro
milestone_by_age_26: Won Apex 2010 at age 16 and Revival of Melee 2 at age 16; became one of the 'Five Gods of Melee'; won EVO 2016; ranked #1 player in the world in 2010, 2017, 2018, and 2019; co-owner of Team Liquid since December 2021 — all milestones before or around age 26.
early_history_summary: DeBiedma was born in Argentina and moved to Orlando, Florida in the mid-1990s. His father was an Argentine diplomat and his mother a flight attendant who became a real estate agent. He discovered Melee through the stepson of his father's co-worker and began competing in 2007 at age 14. He met his lifelong friend and future manager Luis 'Crunch' Rosias in fifth grade. He quickly rose to become the best Smasher in Florida, placing 3rd at GENESIS and winning Apex 2010.
